newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end mostly firmer on light vols.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end mostly firmer on light vols.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended mostly higher Monday, with the exception of silver, but volumes were lighter than seen recently.

"Gold held above Friday's lows, but would need to get back above $350 before anyone would get excited and the market remains concerned about potential European central bank sales," Pioneer Futures analyst Scott Meyers in New York.
COMEX April gold ended up $2.50 an ounce at $348.50, after trading in a $345.60-348.80 range, on estimated total volume of 27,000 lots.

In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $346.40/90, after fixing at $344.30 in London Friday afternoon, up from a new three year low at $343.75 at the Monday morning fix. Spot gold close in New York Friday around $344.10/60.

Speaking at the Davos World Economic Forum in Switzerland, Goldfields of South Africa Ltd chief executive, Alan Wright, said he saw gold trading in a $345-365 range in the next few months, but he also suspected there was a European central bank selling the market.
Without central bank sales though, demand would exceed the supply of gold from mines and recycling, he said.

With the US dollar very strong in recent weeks, and the South African rand stabilizing after last year's slide, the gold price in rand fell to new nine-month lows around 1560 rand Monday, prompting concern about South African producer hedging, analysts said.
But Wright doubted there was much producer hedging occurring with gold down at three year lows.

But Wright said about 60 percent of gold producers could mine gold at under $340 an ounce, another 20 pct had costs between $340 and $360 and "would ride with it (the current price slump), and the remaining 20 pct "may go out of business".
Wright also said the Chinese New Year and Muslim Ramadan holidays at this time of year traditionally lowers gold demand seasonally.
COMEX March silver ended down 1.8 cents at $4.902 an ounce, but well off its session low at $4.840.
"The funds are net long in silver and we should see more gains in the next few weeks with COMEX silver stocks still very low," Meyers said.

In the CFTC Commitment of Traders data for the period ended January 28, released late Friday, non-commercials or funds were net long 10,513 lots in silver, a turnaround from a net short position of 1,889 lots two weeks ago.
In the platinum metals group, NYMEX April platinum ended up $2.90 an ounce at $355.70, after spot platinum saw new three year lows Friday.
NYMEX March palladium ended up $1.85 an ounce at $128.80, continuing its rally of the past six weeks.
"There is speculative interest in palladium and good consumer demand," Johnson Matthey analyst Frank Reddon said.

"The Russian have not shipped any palladium for a month and a half, after budget problems disrupted contract talks with the Japanese, and the Japanese are having to take large quantities out of the spot market," he said.

Russia is a bigger player in the palladium market than in the platinum market, accounting for about 54 percent of total annual palladium supply in 1996, but only around 20 pct on world platinum supply, analysts said.
((--Clive McKeef, New York Commodities Desk, +1-212-859-1641; -email: clive.mckeef@reuters.com))
